overview: China Feihe is China's largest domestic infant formula producer, built around the positioning that its milk powder is "more suitable for the constitution of Chinese babies." The Group manufactures super-premium, premium and regular infant milk formula alongside adult milk powder, liquid milk and other dairy products, selling through a nationwide network of roughly 2,600-2,800 distributors and 67,000-70,000 offline retail points plus e-commerce, with a small U.S. nutritional-supplements retail business (Vitamin World USA) and an early-stage overseas infant formula push via a Canadian production plant. Virtually all revenue and production is concentrated in mainland China, reported in RMB.

business_model.summary: Feihe sells branded infant and toddler milk formula almost entirely through third-party distributors and retail/e-commerce channels, supplemented by adult/other dairy products and a small U.S. vitamins retail chain. Revenue is transactional (repeat consumer staple purchases, not contracted/recurring), driven by birth cohort size, formula pricing/mix, and market share versus multinational and domestic rivals.

revenue_streams.name: Other dairy products (adult milk powder, liquid milk, rice powder supplements)

business_model.customer_type: B2C consumer staple sold through B2B distributor network (73.3% of dairy revenue via ~2,800 offline distributors/retail points) plus direct e-commerce
business_model.geographic_mix: Mainland China >98% of revenue; small Canada production/North America retail presence and nascent Southeast Asia expansion

competitive_position.market_position: Historically the #1 player in China's infant formula market by sales volume/value for six-to-seven consecutive years (per Frost & Sullivan/Euromonitor), though 2025 data is contested: Feihe cites ~17.5% retail share (ahead of Danone's ~14%), while a competing data source puts Yili's 2025 retail share at ~18.3%, implying Yili may have overtaken Feihe. Either way, the market leadership gap has narrowed sharply from Feihe's earlier dominance.

moat_factors.description: Long-standing "more suitable for Chinese babies" positioning and deep rural/lower-tier city distribution give Feihe strong brand recall domestically, reinforced by over 700,000 face-to-face mother/seminar marketing events per year

Self-production of 11 key milk protein ingredients, proprietary fresh-extraction technology and >80% equipment localization reduce reliance on imported milk protein and support a cost/quality narrative, though this has not prevented share and margin erosion
Extensive nationwide network of thousands of distributors and tens of thousands of retail points, particularly strong in lower-tier cities
China's tightened infant formula registration regime (effective 2023) raises entry barriers for new domestic entrants, which somewhat protects incumbents like Feihe

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a single structurally shrinking category (infant formula, ~88% of revenue) with no comparable scale in adjacent categories
Losing share to multinationals (Danone premium lines) and domestic rival Yili, which is growing infant formula and goat-milk formula share aggressively
Thin or negative gross margin in diversification categories (other dairy products gross margin only ~1.0% in FY2025, nutritional supplements ~49% but immaterial scale)
Promotional/subsidy-driven growth (e.g., nationwide maternity giveaway) risks normalizing lower net pricing and training consumers to expect discounts
Limited brand power outside China; overseas (Canada, Southeast Asia, U.S. Vitamin World) remains a small, early-stage contributor

growth_drivers: China's 2025-2026 government childcare subsidy system (RMB3,600/child/year nationwide, ~RMB110bn total 2026 funding) and other pro-natalist measures (free preschool year, local cash subsidies) that could stabilize or modestly lift the newborn base from 2026-2028
Feihe's own RMB1.2bn nationwide maternity/baby-formula subsidy program, intended to defend/grow market share by effectively discounting product to new parents
Premiumization: increasing urbanization, rising disposable income (RMB43,377 per-capita in 2025, 6.1% CAGR 2020-2025) supporting high-end formula demand
Second growth curve into whole-lifecycle nutrition: children's, adolescent, and middle-aged/elderly nutrition products, children's cheese, special dietary powders
Overseas expansion: Canadian plant obtained the first foreign-invested infant formula production permit in the region; accelerating entry into Southeast Asia and growing U.S. retail footprint
Capital returns to shareholders (share buybacks and semi-annual dividends of at least 30% of net profit) supporting per-share value even as absolute profit shrinks
H1 2026 revenue growth turned positive (+2.3% YoY) after several years of decline, a possible early inflection point

business.description: China's number of newborns fell from ~41.9 million children aged 0-3 in 2020 to ~26.5 million in 2025; even with 2025 revenue stabilizing, the addressable market has shrunk roughly 37% over five years
FY2025 infant formula revenue fell 16.8% YoY, management attributing the decline explicitly to 'intensified industry competition'; rivals Yili, Danone and others are gaining ground
87.6% of revenue still from infant milk formula; diversification into other dairy and nutritional supplements remains small and low-margin
Large one-off giveaway/subsidy programs used to defend share could compress net realized pricing and margins industry-wide if sustained or matched by competitors

financial.description: Net income fell from RMB6.9bn (FY2021) to RMB1.9bn (FY2025), a ~72% decline over four years, driven by both revenue decline and margin compression (gross margin 70.3%->65.0%)

financial.risk: Falling interest income on large cash/deposit pile
financial.description: Large wealth management products, structured and long-term bank deposits (RMB8-10bn) generate meaningful 'other income'; FY2025 other income fell 18.2% on lower bank interest income and reduced government subsidies, and H1 2026 other income fell a further 36.0% on lower interest income, a direct hit to the bottom line as China's rates fall
Canadian dollar exposure from the Canada plant; unhedged, though small relative to overall RMB-denominated group

regulatory.description: China's stricter 2021/2023 national infant formula safety standards and revised formula registration regime raise compliance costs but also raise barriers for new entrants, a double-edged risk/benefit
Dividends ultimately depend on distributions from PRC subsidiaries, subject to PRC statutory reserve requirements and potential capital controls
Upside case partly rests on continued/expanded state childcare subsidies and birth-support policy, which could be scaled back or redirected

macro.risk: China's declining birth rate / demographic headwind
macro.description: National birth rate fell from 8.52 per thousand (2020) to 5.63 per thousand (2025); ~7.9 million newborns in 2025 versus a much larger historical base -- this is the dominant secular macro risk to the entire category, independent of company execution
Premiumization thesis depends on continued disposable income growth; a broader consumption slowdown would pressure the high-end/super-premium mix that carries Feihe's best margins

macro.risk: Geopolitical/trade risk on overseas dairy inputs and expansion
macro.description: International milk protein supply tightness was cited as an industry-wide cost pressure; Canada plant exposed to any Canada-China trade friction

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's infant milk formula market in retail sales value is expected by Frost & Sullivan/management commentary to remain broadly stable despite a shrinking 0-3 age cohort, supported by premiumization, rising confidence in domestic brands, and government childcare subsidies; newborn numbers are forecast to improve from 2026-2028 off a low base, but the structural decline since 2016-2017 remains the dominant multi-year trend
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low cyclicality in the traditional economic sense (infant nutrition is a consumer staple/non-discretionary for parents), but highly sensitive to demographic trends (birth cohort size) which act as a structural rather than cyclical swing factor
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate and unusual for a consumer staples company: Feihe holds very large cash, structured deposits and wealth management products (well over RMB15bn combined cash plus term/structured deposits), so falling PRC interest rates directly reduce 'other income' and reported profit, as seen in FY2025 and H1 2026
key_input_costs: Imported and domestic milk protein/raw milk powder

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 revenue rose 2.3% YoY to RMB9.36bn, the first year-on-year revenue increase reported after several years of decline, though net profit still fell 12.7% YoY to RMB901 million on lower other income (interest income down) and higher selling/admin expenses
Non-executive director Kingsley Kwok King Chan resigned from the Board (15 May 2026)

Heavy short-selling activity reported on HKEX (short sales reportedly ~48.7% of turnover on a single August 2026 session), alongside a sharp share price decline (down roughly 30%+ from prior highs during 2026)

FY2025 revenue fell 12.7% YoY to RMB18.1bn and net profit fell 42.7% YoY to RMB1.94bn, driven by a 16.8% decline in infant milk formula revenue amid intensified competition; gross margin compressed from 66.3% to 65.0%

Interim dividend of HK$0.1209/share (~RMB1.0bn) paid September 2025; final FY2025 dividend of HK$0.1290/share (~RMB1.0bn) proposed, together representing over 145% of H2 2025 profit and continuing the policy of distributing no less than 30% of annual net profit

Feihe launched a nationwide maternity/newborn subsidy giveaway (reported cost ~RMB1.2bn, ~6% of revenue) effectively worth over RMB1,500 per eligible family, intended to defend market share against Danone, Yili, Friso and a2 Milk; Citi raised Feihe's net profit forecasts 3% (2025) and 15% (2026) on the news
HSBC maintained a 'Hold' rating, projecting 2.4% revenue CAGR and 5.5% EBIT CAGR 2025-2028, citing Feihe as a likely early beneficiary of Beijing's pro-natalist population policies

Founder/Chairman Leng Youbin's disclosed shareholding was reduced via related-entity restructuring (stakes moved among LYB International Holding/Harneys Trustees entities); unclear whether this reflects open-market selling or estate/trust planning

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (August 2026) / FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026)

items.target: no less than 30% of net profit per financial year
items.notes: Stated minimum payout policy since IPO; FY2025 actual payout (interim + final, ~RMB2.0bn combined) exceeded 100% of H2 2025 profit specifically, reflecting Board discretion to pay above the policy floor

items.target: RMB ~1 billion (2025 program, per interim results commentary)
items.notes: Press reports conflict on magnitude (some cite RMB10bn); the RMB1bn figure aligns better with the company's cash position and the smaller RMB2bn total dividend figure confirmed in the FY2025 annual report, so is more likely accurate, but should be verified against the HKEX buyback announcement

items.target: maintain leading market share and sales volume
items.notes: Management asserts continued #1 position; some third-party retail-tracking data suggests Yili may have taken the lead in 2025 -- methodology-dependent and unresolved
Feihe does not publish formal quantitative revenue or earnings guidance in its filings; HSBC's independent estimate is 2.4% revenue CAGR and 5.5% EBIT CAGR for 2025-2028

guidance.management_commentary: Management's FY2025 letter emphasizes 'long-termism,' continued milk-protein R&D investment, and expansion of a 'whole-lifecycle nutrition' product matrix (infant, children, adolescent, middle-aged/elderly) as a second growth curve intended to smooth the impact of the shrinking birth cohort. Management highlights global expansion (Canada production permit, Southeast Asia entry) as a longer-term diversification lever, while acknowledging in both the FY2025 annual report and H1 2026 interim report that 'intensified industry competition' is the primary driver of continued formula revenue pressure.

bull_case: H1 2026 marks the first year-on-year revenue growth in several years (+2.3%), potentially signaling a bottom in the multi-year infant formula revenue decline

China's 2025-2026 nationwide childcare subsidies (RMB3,600/child/year, ~RMB110bn 2026 funding) and other pro-natalist policies could stabilize or modestly lift newborn numbers from 2026-2028, directly expanding Feihe's addressable market
Still the largest or near-largest domestic player by scale, brand recognition and distribution reach, with genuine vertical integration in milk protein production that smaller rivals lack

Strong balance sheet with minimal debt (RMB420m-733m bank borrowings vs RMB7-7.5bn cash plus several billion more in structured/long-term deposits) and a shareholder-friendly capital return policy (>=30% payout plus buybacks) that can cushion equity returns even if earnings keep shrinking

Optionality from overseas expansion (Canada production permit, Southeast Asia entry, growing U.S. Vitamin World footprint) as a long-dated diversification away from the shrinking domestic birth cohort
bear_case: China's structural decline in births is a multi-year secular headwind that no amount of company execution can fully offset -- the 0-3 age population nearly halved from 2020 to 2025

Losing competitive ground: FY2025 infant formula revenue fell 16.8% and net income is down ~72% from the FY2021 peak, with credible third-party data suggesting rival Yili may have overtaken Feihe in 2025 retail share

Growth strategy increasingly reliant on costly promotional giveaways and subsidies to defend share, which risks training consumers toward discount-driven purchases and compressing category-wide margins over time

Diversification into adjacent categories (other dairy, nutritional supplements) remains small in scale and, in the case of other dairy products, carries very thin gross margins (~1% in FY2025), offering limited near-term offset

Falling PRC interest rates are shrinking the 'other income' contribution from Feihe's large cash/deposit holdings, removing what has been a meaningful profit tailwind in recent years, compounding the core business's earnings decline
